summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of right-sided chest pain with palpitations and worsening chronic abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had uncontrolled type 1 diabetes due to loss of her glucometer and missed insulin doses. Initial workup ruled out myocardial infarction with normal EKGs and troponins. She accidentally dislodged her GJ tube during the admission, requiring temporary Foley placement and subsequent replacement by interventional radiology. A low-grade fever and erythema at the tube site led to a short course of clindamycin, with improvement. Pain was managed with IV Dilaudid and a structured regimen allowing one patient-chosen extra dose daily. Insulin was adjusted with endocrinology input, resulting in a new regimen of 60 units Lantus at bedtime and a sliding scale for Humalog. She improved clinically, maintained oral intake, and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics, follow up with her providers, and manage her diabetes and pain medications appropriately.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
